game: CAR @ ATL Week 11 2025, kickoff 2025-11-16 13:00 ET, Mercedes-Benz Stadium roof closed

script.base: Dome, ATL -4.5, total 42.5, implied ATL 23.5 / CAR 19.0. Most likely a one-score game: Atlanta leads late but does not blow it open, so Bijan Robinson gets the clock carries while Carolina stays run-leaning with Rico Dowdle (51 carries, 237 yards in weeks 8-10, about 17 carries and 79 rush yards a game) rather than a pure dropback script. Moderate pace, not a shootout.
script.flip1: Atlanta gets up by two scores early, grinds with Robinson and Tyler Allgeier, and Carolina abandons the run: Dowdle's rushing line dies and Tetairoa McMillan (24 targets, 256 air yards in weeks 8-10) becomes the usage spike. Blowout also puts Atlanta starter snaps at risk late.
script.flip2: Dowdle plus a short Atlanta front (Leonard Floyd, Josh Woods, Malik Verdon, Sam Roberts out) keeps it tied or gives Carolina the lead, so Michael Penix has to throw to Drake London and Kyle Pitts and both lead backs play full snaps. Alternate flip: Atlanta's OL (Matthew Bergeron out, Chris Lindstrom questionable) stalls drives and the 42.5 goes under in a slog.

injury_fallout: Source: nflverse official pre-game injury report plus weeks 8-10 usage in the pack. Final inactives (~90 min pre-kick) are not in the pack. ATL OUT: LB Leonard Floyd (hamstring), LB Josh Woods (hamstring), CB Dee Alford (concussion), DT Sam Roberts (knee), G Matthew Bergeron (ankle), LB Malik Verdon (shoulder). ATL QUESTIONABLE, not treated as out: WR Drake London (illness), CB Mike Hughes (neck), G Chris Lindstrom (foot), DT Zach Harrison (knee), DT Brandon Dorlus (oblique), WR Jamal Agnew (foot), TE Feleipe Franks (foot). CAR OUT: LB Trevin Wallace (shoulder), S Lathan Ransom (hand). Who gains: Carolina rushers vs a depleted Atlanta front and Alford's absence for McMillan/Xavier Legette; Atlanta pass catchers vs Ransom out, with Pitts (21 targets L3) the healthy co-primary if London is limited. Who loses: Atlanta rush efficiency (Bergeron out, Lindstrom questionable) and Carolina's deep shots if the 45% Atlanta blitz still gets home (Floyd out is only a partial offset). No Carolina skill-position out; Dowdle is already the next man up over Chuba Hubbard (51 carries to 20 in weeks 8-10).

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack (step limitation). Location splits only: ATL allows 7.05 YPA left (94 att), 10.4 middle (45 att), 5.33 right (98 att) over 9 games — middle is the pass bleed on a small sample, right side is stingy. CAR allows 7.22 left (133), 8.68 middle (65), 6.43 right (110) over 10 games.
matchup.pressure: ATL blitz rate 45%; CAR EPA/dropback -0.22 vs blitz and -0.07 with no blitz, so pressure has been getting home on Bryce Young and should cut deep WR yards (McMillan 256 air yards L3). Floyd out may trim that pressure. CAR blitzes only 25%; ATL EPA/dropback is -0.28 when blitzed but +0.07 when not, so Penix should be comfortable in the base shell.
matchup.bleeds: ATL run defense: 5.08 YPC and 33 runs of 10+ over 9 games, now without Floyd, Woods, Verdon and Roberts. That is the clear defensive bleed. CAR run defense is more neutral at 4.60 YPC and 25 runs of 10+ over 10 games, but CAR has allowed more pass explosives (29 plays of 20+, 324 yards) than ATL (19/266).
matchup.overlap: Carolina's primary rusher, Dowdle, runs into the exact ATL bleed (5.08 YPC, depleted front). Carolina's primary receiver, McMillan, is a vertical target into a 45% blitz that has already made this offense worse, so that overlap is blocked even with Alford out and middle YPA 10.4. Atlanta's healthy overlap is Pitts (21 targets, 202 air yards L3) into CAR's soft middle (8.68 YPA) plus Ransom out; London (22/222/238 L3) is the same overlap but questionable with an illness, so he is not a playable leg.

CAR is a 4.5 dog, so the systematic read is Carolina throws more and Atlanta's lead back runs late; a true blowout is the flip, not the base, because the spread is only 4.5. CAR's 19.0 implied points fit a run-to-stay-close script better than a track meet. Hubbard is not the late-clock back in either script.

edge_players.kills_it: Dowdle is scratched or leaves early and Hubbard reclaims the early-season role that set the 62.5 median, or a balanced split of about 12 carries against a front allowing 5.08 YPC turns even backup work into 62-plus.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost. Why: Dowdle was inactive or exited and Hubbard inherited 15-18 carries against a front at 5.08 YPC missing Floyd, Woods, Verdon and Roberts, so Hubbard cleared 62.5 while Dowdle's over never started. Or Carolina was down two scores by halftime, Young threw them out of the run, and Dowdle finished on his 53-yard last-four floor under 53.5 while Hubbard still stayed under — a split that the shared Dowdle-health dependency was built to suffer. Or a more even carry split than 51-to-20, plus one chunk run and a screen, nicked Hubbard over 62.5 without a role change. Closed roof removes weather as the excuse. No saved price means there was also no CLV check if the market had already shaded Hubbard down.
slip_story: One story: Carolina's run game is Dowdle's, not a committee, against a soft Atlanta run defense in a one-score dome game (ATL 23.5 / CAR 19.0). The stack is Dowdle rush yards over with Hubbard rush+rec under. Do not add McMillan, Pitts or London overs — those need the abandon-the-run flip or an Atlanta throw script. Do not add a total under to this same slip. No TDs, one market per player. Two legs only; no third name survived both the base script and a flip.
